newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's future leader regrets Deng missed handover.
newsitem.headline: HK's future leader regrets Deng missed handover.

text.p: Hong Kong's leader-designate, Tung Chee-hwa, voiced his sorrow on Saturday that China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had died without fulfilling his dream of witnessing Beijing's recovery of the territory.
"We had been looking forward to Mr Deng's visit to Hong Kong after our return to our motherland," the official Xinhua news agency quoted shipping magnate Tung as saying.

"To our regret this wish of ours can never be fulfilled," said Tung, who will be Hong Kong's first chief executive after Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 after 150 years as a British colony.

Deng died on Wednesday at 92 but had said he dreamt of being in Hong Kong for the handover, which China's paramount leader brokered, and which Beijing sees as ending a century and a half of colonial humiliation.

Deng's policies had assured a solid foundation for the long-term stability and development of Hong Kong after it returns to China at midnight on June 30, Tung said, praising his "one country, two systems" formula under which Hong Kong's capitalist system is guaranteed for 50 years.
"Mr Deng is most admired and respected by the Hong Kong community," Tung said, extending his condolences to Deng's family.
A shadow legislature to be installed in Hong Kong when Beijing takes over began a meeting in southern China with three minutes of silent tribute to the patriarch.
At the start of the meeting, held across the border in the city of Shenzhen, Provisional Legislature president Rita Fan praised Deng.
The meeting was the second since the 60-member interim body was chosen by a 400-strong Beijing-anointed caucus in December.
The controversial assembly will replace Hong Kong's elected legislature, reversing colonial governor Chris Patten's democratic reforms in the last days of British rule.
